lines.en: Picked up, it was light as paper and smelled faintly sweet. Dry and smooth to the touch.

lines.en: She showed us three photographs from July. On cords strung across the whole garden, freshly peeled kanpyō swayed in the wind.

lines.ja: ユウガオの{大|おお}きい{実|み}を{薄|うす}く{長|なが}く{剥|む}き、{二日|ふつか}ほど{日差|ひざ}しに{当|あ}てて{干|ほ}す。{夏|なつ}の{強|つよ}い{日差|ひざ}しが{不可欠|ふかけつ}なのだ。

lines.en: You peel the big yūgao gourd into thin, long ribbons and dry them in the sun for about two days. Strong summer sunlight is indispensable.

lines.ja: {雨|あめ}が{一度|いちど}でも{降|ふ}れば、ことごとく{駄目|だめ}になる。「だから{夏|なつ}の{間|あいだ}は、{空|そら}ばかり{見|み}ていました」と、{福田|ふくだ}さんは{笑|わら}った。

lines.en: One rain and every strip is ruined. "So all summer I did nothing but watch the sky," Fukuda-san laughed.

lines.ja: {奥|おく}の{台所|だいどころ}では、ケンがかんぴょうを{煮|に}ていた。{醤油|しょうゆ}と{砂糖|さとう}の{匂|にお}いが、{店|みせ}まで{届|とど}いてくる。

lines.en: In the kitchen at the back, Ken was simmering kanpyō. The smell of soy sauce and sugar drifted out into the shop.

lines.en: The kanpyō rolls Fukuda-san made were slender, lined up neatly on the plate. Ken was lost in admiration at her deft hands.

lines.ja: {噛|か}むと、しっとりとした{甘|あま}い{味|あじ}の{奥|おく}に、{去年|きょねん}の{夏|なつ}の{日差|ひざ}しが{余|あま}す{所|ところ}なく{含|ふく}まれていた。

lines.en: Biting in, behind the moist, sweet taste, there was last summer's sunlight, all of it, nothing left out.

lines.ja: このかんぴょうが{庭|にわ}で{干|ほ}されていた{七月|しちがつ}、{私|わたし}たちは{三島|みしま}の{水|みず}を{飲|の}み、{箱根|はこね}の{霧|きり}の{中|なか}を{歩|ある}いていた。

lines.en: Three long pauses; Tanaka-san's dashing about by train; the kitchens Ken borrowed. Start listing them and this page would not be enough.

lines.en: From Nihonbashi, where we saw the cherry blossoms in spring, all the way here, we have passed through forty-nine post towns. We decided to walk, and we have carried it through.

lines.en: That is entirely thanks to the people we met on the road. The "small kindnesses" at the back of the diary grew by one more today.

lines.en: Fukuda-san put hot tea into our cold hands. "You have walked a long way," she said, and I was overcome with gratitude.

lines.en: Tanaka-san took the watch from his pocket. "To Lake Biwa: two post towns and one hill. It is two forty."

lines.en: Tanaka-san looked at the wall too and nodded, satisfied. "This shop's clock is correct."

{三上山|みかみやま}の{向|む}こうには{何|なに}がありますか。

items.recapEn: From the road out of Tsuchiyama Hana saw the first low hills around Lake Biwa; Tanaka-san named Mikami-yama, and she could not hold back what she felt. At Fukuda-san's kanpyō shop in Minakuchi they saw last July's dried strips and drying-rack photographs and ate kanpyō rolls. The shop clock, for once, agreed with Tanaka-san's watch.

lines.en: Go ahead. Don't turn the heat up. People tend to overcook it. It goes tough, so be careful.

items.recapEn: In the shop, Fukuda-san explained the kanpyō was last July's. Hana decided it had waited for them; Ken insisted kanpyō does not wait. He borrowed the kitchen again (Tanaka-san: forget the count, or it becomes debt). Fukuda-san invited them back for the summer drying. Ken: kanpyō doesn't wait, but Lake Biwa does.
